beats.summary: Dwight considers getting a TiVo or DVD burner, commenting on Jim's luck.

evidence.snippet: Dwight: Ooh. They're having a sale on TiVo. Maybe I should get a TiVo. Oh. DVD Burner! Maybe I should get one of those.

beats.summary: Jim is recognized as top salesman and reflects on the honor.

evidence.snippet: Jim: Dwight was the top salesman of the year at our company. He wins a little prize money and gets honored at some convention.

beats.summary: Jim discusses wedding planning and potential awkwardness at work.

evidence.snippet: Pam: I have a ton of stuff to do for the wedding. And I have to do it in the office. And that can be kind of awkward.

beats.summary: Michael prepares Dwight for his big speech at the sales convention.

evidence.snippet: Michael: That's what she said!
Dwight: Well, it's not really a big speech. You still coming right?
Michael: Oh! Abso-fruit-ly. Fruit. Grapes. Nailed the joke. Matter of time. Um… And yes, it is a big speech. Biggest of your life.

beats.summary: Michael shares his past experience with giving speeches and receiving awards.

evidence.snippet: Michael: Speaker at the Sales Convention. Been there, done that. Went there again, did it again. Two years in a row.

beats.summary: Dwight considers giving a long thank you speech, but Michael advises against it.

evidence.snippet: Dwight: What if I give a really long, extended Thank You. For instance, "Thank you, Mr. Blank. Thank you very, very, very…"
Michael: That would look terrible. These are mostly salesmen and salesmen expect to be entertained and you are the main act.

beats.summary: Dwight recounts a childhood spelling bee failure, expressing doubt about public speaking.

evidence.snippet: Dwight: When I was in the sixth grade, I was a finalist in our school Spelling Bee. It was me against Raj Patel. And I misspelled, in front of the entire school, the word 'failure'.

beats.summary: Michael offers to teach Dwight enough to avoid embarrassment at the speech.

evidence.snippet: Michael: But I can teach you enough so that you don't embarrass me or the company.
Dwight: Okay, deal! I'll do whatever you say. No questions asked.

beats.summary: Michael makes a joke about the difference between salesmen and saleswomen.

evidence.snippet: Michael (stand up comic voice): But seriously, what's the difference between a salesman and a saleswoman?
Dwight: Saleswoman has a vagina.
Michael: It's a joke, Dwight. It's not a Sex Ed class.
Dwight: But I'm right?
Michael: Yeah, you're right about the difference between a man and a woman, but not about the punch line to the joke, right? The difference between a salesman and a saleswoman… is boobs!

beats.summary: Michael boasts about his ability to command an audience and his past success with bonuses.

evidence.snippet: Michael: I do. Both of them.
